{"title": "Spiney Swims in the Stream", "level": 2, "topic": "spinosaurus", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Long ago, a dino named Spiney lived by a stream. Spiney was the biggest meat eater of all!

Each day, Spiney waded in. The water was cool. Its big sail rose up like a boat sail.

Spiney did not chase big beasts on the plain. Spiney ate fish!

It kept still. It did not make a sound. Then — snap! A fish for a meal.

A small dino peeked from the reeds. "Teach me!" she said.

"Stay low," said Spiney. "Wait. Do not speak. Fish can feel you coming."

The small dino waited. She kept her feet still. Soon she got a fish too!

"I did it!" she squeaked.

Spiney and the small dino ate by the stream. The sun beamed on the deep green water.

Maya reads this and dreams of that day.", "cover_scene": "A huge sail-backed Spinosaurus standing in a green river catching a fish, with a small dinosaur watching from the tall reeds."}

She lifted the lid. A bright beam shot out!

Whoosh! Maya sat on hot sand. Palm trees swayed. A stream ran by.

"Where am I?" she said.

A guide in a green coat waved. "You are in Africa. This is long ago — one hundred million years!"

Maya saw a huge tail in the stream. A sail rose from the water.

"Spiney!" she said. "The biggest meat eater of all!"

Spiney did not need Maya. Spiney wanted fish. Snap! It ate its meal and waded away.

"Stay near me," said the guide. "Keep your feet on this trail."

They saw green leaves, deep mud, and a road of stone.

Then — whoosh! Maya was home again. She held one small gray scale.", "cover_scene": "A girl in shorts standing on sandy ground by a river in a prehistoric landscape, watching a huge sail-backed dinosaur in the water, palm trees behind."}

{"title": "The Baby Dino in the Reeds", "level": 2, "topic": "baby dinosaur", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Fern heard a small peep by the reeds.

"Peep! Peep!"

Fern leaned down. A baby dino sat in the green reeds. It was alone.

"Do not be afraid," said Fern. "I will help you."

Coal came down the road. Rain came too. The team looked at the baby.

"It needs to eat," said Coal.

Fern reached up and got soft leaves. The baby ate each one. Munch, munch!

"Now it needs its mom," said Rain.

So the team walked the trail by the sea. They called and called.

Then a big shape rose near the oak trees. It was the baby's mom! She had a long neck and kind eyes.

"Thank you," she said.

The baby peeped and ran to her.

Fern, Coal, and Rain waved. They felt warm inside all day.", "cover_scene": "Three friendly dinosaurs leaning over a tiny baby dinosaur sitting in tall green reeds near a sunny shore."}

{"title": "Rain's Big Morning", "level": 2, "topic": "baby dinos", "target_skill": "vowel_teams", "text": "Three baby dinos woke at dawn. Peep! Peep! Peep!

Rain rubbed her eyes. "Oh no. They are all awake!"

The first baby wanted to eat. Rain got green leaves. The baby ate each one.

The next baby wanted a drink. Rain led him to the stream. He drank and drank.

The last baby cried and cried. Rain did not know why.

"Are you cold? Are you afraid?"

Rain held him close. She sang a low, sweet tune. Soon he was still.

Then a loud roar came from the road! A huge T. rex! But it was just big Coal. He was awake too.

"Do you need help?" Coal said.

"Yes, please!" said Rain.

Coal gave each baby a ride on his tail. The babies squeaked with glee.

The sun beamed. What a fine morning!", "cover_scene": "A small dinosaur in the morning sun tending three squeaky baby dinosaurs while a big friendly dinosaur gives one a ride on his tail."}
Noted.

transcript.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
transcript.text:
Maya reads a book about dinosaurs. The book is a real treat!

A green dino eats leaves by the sea. Her name is Fern. She can reach the tall trees. Munch, munch! Leaves taste sweet.

A big dino named Coal rests on the road of sand. He has a long tail. His feet make deep tracks.

"Wait for me!" peeps a small dino. Her name is Rain. She can sail on a log! The log floats on the waves.

Fern, Coal, and Rain are a team. They eat and play each day by the sea.

Then rain falls. Drip, drip! The team runs to a cave. They sit and wait. Soon the sun beams again.

Maya reads the last page. Real dino bones lay deep in the ground. She dreams of a dig one day.

"Dinosaurs are neat!" says Maya.
transcript.cover_scene: Three friendly cartoon dinosaurs — a tall green one eating leaves, a big brown one on the sand, and a small one riding a floating log — beside a sunny blue sea.

chapters.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
chapters.text:
Maya has a dream. She digs by the sea.

She sees a big bone in the sand. It is real!

"This is a dino leg!" says Maya. "It is neat!"

Her team runs to the beach. They dig deep.

They find a jaw. They find teeth. Big teeth!

"Wait," says Jean. "Look at this tail!"

The bones need soap and rain to get clean.

Maya reads a book about dinosaurs. It says some dinos ate meat. Some ate leaves and green plants.

"My dino ate meat," says Maya. "See the teeth?"

The team paints each bone. They keep each one safe.

Soon the dino will stand tall for kids to see.

Maya feels proud. She made a dream come true.

"Each day we learn more," says Maya. "Real scientists still find new dinosaurs today!"

The sun sets. The sea is calm.

Maya waves at her dino. "See you at dawn!"
chapters.cover_scene: A girl in a sun hat kneels on a sandy beach brushing sand off a huge dinosaur jaw with big teeth, waves and cliffs behind her.

transcript.title: Coal the Dino Digs a Trail
transcript.text:
Coal the dino likes to dig. He digs a trail in the soil.

"What can I find?" says Coal.

He digs by the oak tree. He digs by the road. Dirt flies! His tail sweeps the dirt away.

Rain falls on the trail. Drip, drip. Coal does not quit. He digs in the rain.

Then Coal sees it. A big bone! It is white as a sail.

"Fern! Rain! Come see!" Coal calls.

Fern and Rain run to the trail. The team peeks at the bone.

"It is so old," says Fern. "It lay deep in the soil for a long, long time."

Real kids can read about bones like this. Books tell us facts about dinosaurs each day.

Coal sets the bone on a leaf. The sun beams down. The team cheers!

"We can dig again at dawn," says Coal.
transcript.cover_scene: A big brown dinosaur digging in muddy soil with his tail, uncovering a large white bone under an oak tree while two smaller dinosaurs peek from behind.

chapters.title: Rain on the Dino Trail
chapters.text:
Rain fell on the dino trail. Big drops. Loud drops.

A green dino named Oak had a goal. He had to reach his nest by day's end.

"Wait for me!" said Tail. Tail was small and fast.

The two went up the road. They leaped on a boat to float past the deep lake. The sail went flap, flap, flap.

Oak ate green leaves. Tail ate oats and beans.

Soon the rain went away. The sun came out. Oak could see the coast!

"We made it!" said Tail.

The nest was safe. Three eggs lay in the hay. Oak gave a loud roar of joy.

Did you know? Real kids can read dino facts and play dino games at Nat Geo Kids. New dino bones are found each year!

Oak and Tail sat in the last sun beam. They had a good, good day.

transcript.title: Rain Makes a Fossil Trail
transcript.text:
Rain is a small dino. She has a plan today.

"I will make a fossil trail!" she peeps.

Rain steps in soft clay by the sea. Her feet leave neat prints. One, two, three!

Fern eats leaves near the oak tree. "What a great trail!" says Fern.

Coal peeks at the prints. "Wait! Will they stay?"

"Yes," says Rain. "The sun will bake the clay. The prints will not fade away."

Days pass. Weeks pass. The clay turns to stone. The prints stay deep in the stone.

One day, kids find the trail! They see each print in the road of stone.

"A real fossil!" they cheer. "A dino did walk here!"

Maya sees a video about fossils. She learns that prints can last a long time.

Rain was right. Her trail did stay.

chapters.title: The Dino Boat on the Lake
chapters.text:
Dean the dino had a big green boat.

"Can it float?" said Jean.

"It can float!" said Dean.

They set the boat on the lake at dawn. The sun made the water gleam.

Dean had a snack. He ate a peach. Jean ate beans and a leaf of green kale.

Then they saw a shape in the deep lake. It made a big wave!

"Is it a beast?" said Jean.

It was a baby dino! She had a long neck and a sweet squeak.

"Do not be afraid," said Dean. "We will teach you to swim near the boat."

The baby swam. She did not sink. She made a clean, neat path in the lake.

At sunset, the team sailed home.

Real kids can read about dinos too! Scientists still dig up new dino bones each year. Each bone can teach us a neat fact.

transcript.title: Fern Goes to the Museum
transcript.text:
Maya takes a train to the museum today.

The train goes down the rail. Clack, clack! Maya eats a snack on the seat.

At the museum, Maya sees a huge dino. It is made of real bones! The head is up high. The tail goes way down the hall.

"Wow!" says Maya. "It must eat so many leaves!"

A lady in a coat waves. "I dig for bones," she says. "My team finds them deep in the ground."

She lets Maya hold a claw. It feels cold and smooth.

"Can I be on your team?" Maya asks.

"Yes! Read, draw, and play the games. Soon you will know each dino by name."

Maya beams. On the train home, she draws a green dino named Fern. Fern eats leaves by the sea.

Maya can not wait to go again.
transcript.cover_scene: A young girl gazing up at a towering dinosaur skeleton in a bright museum hall, holding a sketchbook.

chapters.title: The Dino Snail Race
chapters.text:
Meet Pea. Pea is a big green dino.

Meet Snail. Snail is small and slow.

"Let's race!" said Pea. "Down the trail to the oak tree!"

Snail did not speak. Snail just went. Slow. Slow. Slow.

Pea ran fast. Then Pea saw a treat. Pea ate leaves. Pea ate beans. Pea ate a peach!

Then Pea took a nap in the heat.

Snail went up the trail. Snail went past the oats. Snail went past the goat.

Soon Snail made it to the oak tree!

Pea woke up. "Oh no!" Pea said. Pea ran to the tree.

Snail beat Pea!

"You are slow but you do not stop," said Pea.

"Slow and steady," said Snail.

Did you know? Real scientists read dino bones like a team reads a map. They learn what each dino ate, and they teach us each year!

Pea and Snail sat and had a snack of leaves.
chapters.cover_scene: A big friendly green dinosaur crouching nose-to-nose with a tiny smiling snail at the start of a dirt trail, with a tall oak tree far in the distance.

chapters.title: The Dino Team Eats a Feast
chapters.text:
The dino team had a big meal today.

Rex ate green leaves from a tall tree. He ate leaf after leaf. Each leaf was a treat.

"Eat with me!" said Rex.

Soap the small dino did not eat leaves. She ate beans and peas by the road.

A goat came down the lane. The goat ate oats from a bowl.

"This is a feast!" said Rex. "A dino feast!"

They ate on the beach. They ate in the rain. The rain did not stop the team.

Rain fell on each leaf. Rain fell on the oats. The team just ate and ate.

Then they read a book about dinosaurs. The book said real dinosaurs ate leaves and meat long ago. Scientists still find new dino bones today!

"We eat like real dinosaurs," said Rex.

Soap said, "Then let us eat one more leaf!"

And they did.

chapters.title: The Dino Trail by the Sea
chapters.text:
Rain fell on the green trail. A small dino named Pea ran fast.

She would meet her pal Bean by the sea.

"Wait for me!" Pea said. "I need to see the sea!"

Bean sat on a big gray rock. He ate a leaf. He ate a bean.

"Sit down and eat," Bean said. "Then we can play."

Pea ate a leaf too. It was sweet.

The sun came out. The rain went away. The sea was clean and blue.

They ran on the sand. They dug deep. Deep in the sand, Pea saw a bone!

"Is it real?" said Bean.

"It is real," said Pea. "An old dino bone!"

Scientists find bones like this. They read the bones to learn about dinos long ago. Kids can read those facts too.

Pea and Bean sat by the sea. The day was neat.

"Team Pea and Bean!" they said.

transcript.title: Spiney Swims in the Stream
transcript.text:
Long ago, a dino named Spiney lived by a stream. Spiney was the biggest meat eater of all!

Each day, Spiney waded in. The water was cool. Its big sail rose up like a boat sail.

Spiney did not chase big beasts on the plain. Spiney ate fish!

It kept still. It did not make a sound. Then — snap! A fish for a meal.

A small dino peeked from the reeds. "Teach me!" she said.

"Stay low," said Spiney. "Wait. Do not speak. Fish can feel you coming."

The small dino waited. She kept her feet still. Soon she got a fish too!

"I did it!" she squeaked.

Spiney and the small dino ate by the stream. The sun beamed on the deep green water.

Maya reads this and dreams of that day.
transcript.cover_scene: A huge sail-backed Spinosaurus standing in a green river catching a fish, with a small dinosaur watching from the tall reeds.

chapters.title: Dino Rain on the Road
chapters.text:
Rain! Rain fell on the road.

A big dino had a raincoat. Her name was Gail.

"I will wait," said Gail. "Rain is not bad."

A small dino ran up the road. His name was Boat, and he had no raincoat.

"Wait for me!" said Boat.

Gail made room. Boat got under her raincoat. The rain fell, but they did not get soaked.

They ate a snack in the rain. Gail ate leaves. Boat ate beans.

Then the rain went away. The sun made the road dry.

A rainbow sat in the sky!

"Look!" said Boat. "A rainbow!"

Gail and Boat ran down the road to the rainbow.

Did real dinos see rain? Yes! Real dinos saw rain, and sun, and big trees. We read about them and learn new things each day.

Gail and Boat did not read. They ran in the sun.

transcript.title: Maya's Trip to Long Ago
transcript.text:
Maya found a box under the stairs. She read the word on the lid: LONG AGO.

She lifted the lid. A bright beam shot out!

Whoosh! Maya sat on hot sand. Palm trees swayed. A stream ran by.

"Where am I?" she said.

A guide in a green coat waved. "You are in Africa. This is long ago — one hundred million years!"

Maya saw a huge tail in the stream. A sail rose from the water.

"Spiney!" she said. "The biggest meat eater of all!"

Spiney did not need Maya. Spiney wanted fish. Snap! It ate its meal and waded away.

"Stay near me," said the guide. "Keep your feet on this trail."

They saw green leaves, deep mud, and a road of stone.

Then — whoosh! Maya was home again. She held one small gray scale.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl in shorts standing on sandy ground by a river in a prehistoric landscape, watching a huge sail-backed dinosaur in the water, palm trees behind.

chapters.title: Neel the Dino Reads the News
chapters.text:
Neel the dino did not like to read. "They say reading is hard," he said. "I need a reason to read."

His friend Jean had a big green book. "This book is full of dinosaur news," she said. "Scientists dig deep and clean each bone. Then they teach us what they see."

Neel took a seat by the stream. He read each page slowly. He read that some dinosaurs had beaks. He read that some ate leaves, and some ate meat. He read that the sea had giant beasts too, but they were not true dinosaurs.

"They keep finding more!" Neel said. "Real teams of scientists find new bones each year."

Jean did not speak. She just smiled.

By the end of the week, Neel read the whole book. Then he read it again, and the words did not feel slow. They felt easy.

"I am a reader," said Neel. "Indeed I am."

transcript.title: The Baby Dino in the Reeds
transcript.text:
Fern heard a small peep by the reeds.

"Peep! Peep!"

Fern leaned down. A baby dino sat in the green reeds. It was alone.

"Do not be afraid," said Fern. "I will help you."

Coal came down the road. Rain came too. The team looked at the baby.

"It needs to eat," said Coal.

Fern reached up and got soft leaves. The baby ate each one. Munch, munch!

"Now it needs its mom," said Rain.

So the team walked the trail by the sea. They called and called.

Then a big shape rose near the oak trees. It was the baby's mom! She had a long neck and kind eyes.

"Thank you," she said.

The baby peeped and ran to her.

Fern, Coal, and Rain waved. They felt warm inside all day.
transcript.cover_scene: Three friendly dinosaurs leaning over a tiny baby dinosaur sitting in tall green reeds near a sunny shore.

chapters.title: They Said the Dino Did Not Dig
chapters.text:
Maya found a bone in the yard, and they all came to look.

"A dino did this!" said Gail. "A big one dug the hole."

"They did not," said Neel. "The dino did not dig at all. The rain did."

So they did what smart kids do. They read. On a science page for kids, they saw facts, art, and games about dinosaurs that lived long ago.

The page said that many dinosaurs did not dig. They walked, they ran, and they ate leaves by the lake. But some small ones did dig safe dens for their eggs.

"So they did dig!" said Gail. "Just not the big ones."

"The bone is not a dino bone," said Neel. "It is from the dog next door."

They all sat and said nothing. Then they did laugh, loud and long.

"The dog did dig," said Maya. "But the facts did win."

transcript.title: Rain's Big Morning
transcript.text:
Three baby dinos woke at dawn. Peep! Peep! Peep!

Rain rubbed her eyes. "Oh no. They are all awake!"

The first baby wanted to eat. Rain got green leaves. The baby ate each one.

The next baby wanted a drink. Rain led him to the stream. He drank and drank.

The last baby cried and cried. Rain did not know why.

"Are you cold? Are you afraid?"

Rain held him close. She sang a low, sweet tune. Soon he was still.

Then a loud roar came from the road! A huge T. rex! But it was just big Coal. He was awake too.

"Do you need help?" Coal said.

"Yes, please!" said Rain.

Coal gave each baby a ride on his tail. The babies squeaked with glee.

The sun beamed. What a fine morning!

chapters.title: The Dino Who Said Yes
chapters.text:
They said the big dino did not play.
They said he did not hop.
But the dino said, "Yes! I can!"

Maya read the dino news. The news said dinos ran fast. The news said they had long tails. She said, "They did so much!"

The dino did hop. The dino did run. They all said, "Look! Look!"

They said the dino did not sing. The dino said, "Yes! I do!"
He did sing. They did clap.

The sun went down. They said good night. The dino did not go. He said, "One more song."

Maya said, "They were wrong. You did it all!"
The dino said, "Yes. I did."

They said the best thing last:
"They did not know you. Now they do!"
